nahhas-irab:1-1.t: يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ: a naʿt (adjective) of «أيّ». If you pronounce it with hamza, it is derived from «أنبأ», i.e. "to inform". If you do not pronounce the hamza, it may be from «أنبأ» with the hamza lightened, and there is a subtle point of Arabic in this: when the hamza is lightened and a quiescent letter precedes it, the rule is that its vowel is thrown onto what precedes it, but that is not permissible here. The reason for this is that this yāʾ is never vowelled in any circumstances, so since it could not be vowelled, «نبيّ» and «خطيّة» were said; if it were according to analogy, «خطيّة» would be said [Translator's note: the text repeats «خطيّة»; presumably a different form was intended]. If you derive it from «نبا ينبو», it has no hamza and the final yāʾ is converted from a wāw. إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ: that is, when you intend that; and this is figurative (majāz). As for the discussion of إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ when before it is يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ, we have mentioned several views about it. It has also been said: it is addressing the Prophet ﷺ with the plural form out of reverence for him, just as one says to an eminent man "you (pl.) did". The meaning is: when you divorce the women with whom you have consummated marriage. فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made this clear on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ: that it is divorce in a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her. وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ: al-Suddī said: that is, keep count of it. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ: that is, do not go beyond what He has commanded you. لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلا يَخْرُجْنَ: then He made an exception: إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative. The scholars disagreed about what this indecency (fāḥisha) is. Among the most comprehensive things said about it is that it is disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; this includes every view, because if she commits fornication or steals and is taken out to have the ḥadd punishment carried out, that is included in this, and likewise if she is foul-mouthed or rebellious. وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ: that is, the things He has defined regarding divorce, the waiting period, and that the wife is not to go out. وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: the alif was dropped for the jussive. فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ: it has been said: that is, he has deprived it of what had been permitted to him, because if he divorces her three times, in whatever circumstance, it is not lawful for him to take her back until she marries another husband; so he has wronged himself by this act. لا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً: most of the exegetes hold that the meaning is that if he divorces her once it is better for him: لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً, namely love for her.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
فَإِذا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ: that is, when they are close to that. فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: that is, with what is due to them from you of maintenance, refraining from foul speech and so on. أَوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: by handing over their dowries to them and what is due to them. وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ: most of the exegetes hold that this concerns taking back (al-rajʿa). From Ibn ʿAbbās: he should take witnesses to the divorce and the taking back, except that if he does not take witnesses, nothing is held against him. وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ: that is, bear witness to the truth when you testify and when you deliver testimony, as al-Suddī said: that is, in the truth.
ذلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ: «ذلكم» addresses a plurality and speaks of a single thing, because the end of the word is for the one you address, and its beginning is for what you speak of or ask about. وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً: the exegetes hold that the meaning is that if he fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and divorces once, he has a way out: if he wishes to remarry [her], he remarries; but if he does not fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and divorces three times, he has no way out. This view is soundly reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn ʿAbbās with chains of transmission that cannot be rejected. Ibn ʿUlayya reported from Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Mujāhid, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when a man came to him and said: "O Ibn ʿAbbās, I have divorced my wife three times." Ibn ʿAbbās lowered his head for a long while, then raised his head to the man and said:
"One of you commits a piece of folly and then says: 'O Ibn ʿAbbās!' You divorced three times, so she has become unlawful to you until she marries a husband other than you, and Allah has not made a way out for you; had you feared Him, He would have made a way out for you (pl.)." Then he recited: وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً. And the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, whose authenticity cannot be rejected, is that he said, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning [the declaration] "unlawful" (al-ḥarām): it counts as three; she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ: Qatāda said: from where he does not hope or expect. وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ: that is, his sufficiency; «أحسبني الشيءُ» means "the thing sufficed me". This is the end of the statement; then He said: إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ. Masrūq said: that is, He accomplishes His purpose whether one relies on Him or not, i.e. His decree is carried out. Hārūn the reciter said: in [the reading of] ʿIṣma it is read إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ [i.e. «بالغٌ أمرَه»] [Translator's note: the variant reading is not visible in the vowelled text, which reproduces the standard reading]; and this [the standard reading] is with the tanwīn dropped for lightness. Al-Farrāʾ permitted إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ [i.e. «بالغٌ أمرُه»] with the nominative [of «أمر»] as the agent of «بالغ»; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of «إنّ». قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً: that is, [He has set] for divorce and the waiting period a limit at which they end.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: اللَّائِي is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). So whoever makes «إن ارتبتم» attached to His saying لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ, for him the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ. And whoever takes the construction according to what is reported — that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "O Messenger of Allah, the young and the old who have despaired of menstruation, and وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ, their waiting period has not been mentioned in the Qur'an", whereupon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: وَاللَّائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ (the verse) — says: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is «إن ارتبتم» and what follows it, and the meaning is: if you do not know and are in doubt about their waiting period, their ruling is this. As for the view of ʿIkrima on the meaning of «إن ارتبتم», that it is "if you are in doubt about the blood and do not know whether it is menstrual blood or irregular bleeding (istiḥāḍa)", فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ — this has been refuted from more than one angle. That is because if the doubt were about the blood, it would have been said «إن ارتبتنّ» (if you women are in doubt), because doubt about blood belongs to the women. Also, despair (al-yaʾs) in Arabic is the cutting off of hope, while doubt (al-irtiyāb) is the existence of hope, so it is impossible for them to coexist. وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ: conjoined to the first; the statement is complete. Then He said: وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ. Abū Jaʿfar said: there are two views about this. One of them is that it applies to every pregnant woman, whether divorced after consummation or widowed: when she gives birth, she becomes lawful [to marry]; this is the view of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb [and] Ibn Masʿūd [Translator's note: the text reads «أبيّ بن كعب بن مسعود»; a "wa-" (and) seems to have dropped out]. The second view is that this applies to divorced women only, and that the widow, if she gives birth before the end of four months and ten days, does not become lawful until four months and ten days have passed; likewise, if four months have passed and she has not given birth, she does not become lawful until she gives birth. This is the view of ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. The first view is more appropriate to the apparent sense of the words, because He, Mighty and Majestic, said وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ in general terms, and no specification occurs except by authoritative instruction (tawqīf) from the Messenger ﷺ. أُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ. أَجَلُهُنَّ: a second mubtadaʾ. أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ: the khabar of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. «أجلهنّ» may also be a badal (substitute) from «أولاتُ», with the khabar being «أن يضعن حملهنّ». وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً: the exegetes hold that the meaning is: whoever fears Allah when he wants to divorce, and divorces once as was defined for him, يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً, in that remarrying [her] is lawful for him — unlike someone who divorced three times.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: ذلِكَ: that is, that which has been mentioned regarding divorce, menstruation and the waiting periods. أَمْرُ اللَّهِ أَنْزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ: so that you follow it. وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ: that is, fears Him by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden. يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ: that is, He erases his sins. وَيُعْظِمْ لَهُ أَجْراً: that is, He makes his reward abundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: we know of no one who read it other than this way, contrary to the expression «أعظم الله أجرك» (may Allah make your reward great).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ: it has been said that this pronoun refers back to the women in general with whom marriage has been consummated; and it has been said: to women divorced fewer than three times, and that women divorced three times have neither lodging nor maintenance. On that, the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ is sound: al-Awzāʿī reported it from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama, from Fāṭima bint Qays, from the Prophet ﷺ. This is also inferred from His saying: وَإِنْ كُنَّ أُولاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّى يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ, for He singled out the pregnant women alone; and also, when they are divorced three times they are strangers [to him]. فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ: a condition and its apodosis (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh). وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: Sufyān said: that is, let some of you urge others. وَإِنْ تَعاسَرْتُمْ: al-Suddī said: that is, if the divorced woman says "I will not nurse him", she is not compelled. The Exalted said: فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرى.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ: the lām of command comes with kasra in its basic form, and is made quiescent in فَلْيُنْفِقْ because it is joined to the fāʾ; kasra is also permissible there. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «ومن قُدِرَ عليه رزقُه فلينفقِ مما آتاه الله» [with kasra on the lām], i.e. according to the measure of the straitened provision Allah has given him. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās [on] فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتاهُ اللَّهُ: if he has household goods he can sell, he sells them and spends [the proceeds]. لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا ما آتاها: al-Suddī said: Allah does not burden the poor man with the maintenance of the rich. Ibn Zayd said: He does not burden the poor man with paying zakat and giving alms. سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْراً: that is, either in this world or in the Hereafter, so that the believers may be encouraged to do good.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: «أيّ» is in the genitive by the kāf, and «كأيّن» has come to mean «كم» (how many) for multitude. The meaning is: "and how many people of a town were insolent towards the command of their Lord"; then the muḍāf ilayhi was set in place of the muḍāf. Ibn Zayd said: «عتوا» here means they disobeyed and disbelieved. «العتوّ» in the language is going too far in opposition and disobedience. ʿAmr ibn Abī Salama reported from ʿUmar ibn Sulaymān regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّها (the verse): he said: these are a people who were punished concerning divorce. فَحاسَبْناها: that is, regarding the favours and gratitude. حِساباً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). شَدِيداً: its naʿt (adjective). Ibn Zayd said: the severe reckoning is that in which there is no pardon at all. وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً: that is, not usual. Al-Farrāʾ said: it involves putting first and putting later (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. "We punished it with a terrible punishment in this world, and We will reckon with it a severe reckoning in the Hereafter".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: فَذاقَتْ وَبالَ أَمْرِها: al-Suddī said: that is, the punishment of its conduct; and its conduct was disbelief and disobedience. وَكانَ عاقِبَةُ أَمْرِها خُسْراً: that is, loss, because they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for a paltry share of this world by following their desires.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً: and that is the punishment of the Fire. فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ: a vocative of a muḍāf. والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي الألباب». قَدْ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً: al-Suddī said: the reminder (al-dhikr) is the Qur'an, and the messenger is Muḥammad ﷺ. The implied construction in Arabic on this view is "a reminder possessing a messenger", then [the muḍāf] was omitted, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. It is also possible that «رسول» has the meaning of «رسالة» (message), like أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ
[Maryam: 19], so that «رسولا» would be a badal (substitute) from «ذكر». It is also possible that the implied construction is "We sent a messenger", what preceded in the speech indicating the implied [verb]. Outside the Qur'an, «رسولٌ» in the nominative would be permissible, because «ذكرا» is the end of a verse, and a fresh start after the like of this is better, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُماتٍ لا يُبْصِرُونَ صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ [al-Baqara: 17, 18], and likewise إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ [al-Tawba: 11] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is al-Tawba: 111]; then when the verse was complete He, Mighty and Majestic, said: التَّائِبُونَ الْعابِدُونَ [al-Tawba: 111, 112]; and likewise ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [al-Burūj: 16] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verses are al-Burūj: 15–16].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
يَتْلُوا عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّناتٍ: a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول». لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ: that is, from disbelief to faith. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ: jussive by the condition. وَيَعْمَلْ: conjoined to it; it may be nominative as being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). صالِحاً: that is, in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). خالِدِينَ فِيها: as a ḥāl. أَبَداً: an adverb of time. قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقاً: that is, He has made ample for him his food and drink.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ: the name of Allah the Exalted may be a badal (substitute), or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), with «الذي» a naʿt (adjective); it may also be that «اللهُ [الذي] خلق سبع سماوات» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate). وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ: conjoined. Abū Ḥātim reported that ʿĀṣim read وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ [i.e. «مثلُهنّ»], cutting it off from the first and putting it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described.] يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ: it has been said that the pronoun refers back to the heavens. Most commonly in the speech of the Arabs, what is with the hāʾ and nūn (-hunna) is for a small number; so on this basis the pronoun refers back to the heavens. According to the view of Mujāhid, it refers back to the heavens and the earth. لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: the lām of purpose (lām kay) may be attached to «يتنزّل», or it may be attached to «خلق», i.e. He created the heavens and the earth so that you might know the full extent of His power and authority, and that nothing He wants is impossible for Him and nothing He wills resists Him. وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً: that is, and so that you may know, along with your knowledge of His power, that He knows everything His creatures do; so beware, you who oppose His command, of His assault, because of His power over you and because He knows what you do. Making the name explicit was permissible: He did not say «وأنه» (and that He) but said «وأنّ اللهَ», which is more majestic. On this basis the poet's saying is interpreted: [al-Khafīf] 495-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I see that nothing outruns death; death has spoiled [life] for the rich and the poor alike.)
